messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO burn alert - service="inference-serving" | burn_rate=4.2x over 5m window. severity=page. triggered at 2719003571
alex: I’m on it. paging now. any known deploys or config changes?
maria: not that I can see in deploy logs. infra autoscale bumped a few pods earlier but no model change. checking customer impact now.
jamal: quick check — are we seeing errors or just latency?
product-ops: customers reporting intermittent timeouts to embeddings endpoint via support ticket #INC-1287. severity appears limited to some EU hosts.
alex: OK scope = embeddings path, region=eu-west. is KV cache pressure possible? asking infra.
sre-runbook-bot: runbook: https://intra/runbooks/slo-burn -> suggested actions: 1) confirm error % 2) mute noisy low-impact rules 3) open coordination thread
incident-bot: :information_source: Current metrics snapshot attached (p95 latency, error-rate, token throughput). error_rate(spans): 0.34% overall, 1.6% for embeddings in eu-west.
maria: customer-impacted traffic appears to be about 0.4% of total requests but concentrated on 3 tenants. those tenants match support list.
taylor: proposal: adjust burn alert sensitivity to avoid paging for brief spikes from single endpoints. specifically: require multi-window confirmation (5m AND 30m) OR error > 0.5% among customer traffic.
jamal: agree. also we should reduce noise by excluding non-customer internal health-check traffic label (service:probe) from the alert query.
alex: can we show the actual alert rule?
jamal: paste the current prom rule snippet:
```
- alert: SLOBurn_Inference_Short
  expr: sum(rate(slo_burn_count{service="inference-serving"}[5m])) / sum(slo_target_count[5m]) > 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High SLO burn for inference-serving"
```

jamal: suggested change (temporary hotfix):
```
- alert: SLOBurn_Inference_MultiWindow
  expr: (
    (sum(rate(slo_burn_count{service="inference-serving", traffic_type!="probe"}[5m])) / sum(slo_target_count{traffic_type!="probe"}[5m]) > 4)
    and
    (sum(rate(slo_burn_count{service="inference-serving", traffic_type!="probe"}[30m])) / sum(slo_target_count{traffic_type!="probe"}[30m]) > 1.5)
  )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained SLO burn (multi-window) - inference-serving"
```

maria: that looks reasonable. second condition catches sustained medium burn rather than a 1-off spike. also add an annotation to surface affected tenants with topk by tenant label.
product-ops: +1 — and please post a support notice for the 3 affected tenants once we have rollback/mitigation progress.
alex: immediate mitigations: 1) scale embeddings workers in eu-west by +30% (started) 2) enable fallback model for embeddings for affected tenants (config flag flip queued) 3) disable non-customer probes from alert query (proposed change).
taylor: about paging criteria — if we implement multi-window, do we want to still page ops on 1) any error_rate > 0.5% for >5m for top tenants OR 2) sustained burn per the new rule. my vote: keep tenant-targeted paging separate and stricter threshold.
jamal: agree. implement tenant-targeted alert with label_filter tenant in (top_n) and for: 5m with severity: page. everything else -> severity: ticket.
product-ops: can we also add a temporary dashboard panel that shows impacted tenants, request rates, and latency distribution for embeddings in eu-west? support wants a single link to monitor.
maria: creating dashboard now -> grafana link will be posted shortly.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation steps logged. escalation paused until we see whether new scaling helps. next check in 10m.
(10 minutes pass)
alex: check-in — scaling reduced p95 by ~18%, embeddings error rate in eu-west dropped to 0.9% (was 1.6%). still above target but trending down.
maria: affected tenants error rates: T-123 0.6%, T-456 0.3%, T-789 0.2%. support notified for T-123 and T-456.
taylor: propose final decision for post-incident tuning:
- keep multi-window rule as primary alert (as jamal proposed)
- create tenant-level page rule: error_rate_by_tenant > 0.5% for 5m -> page
- downgrade single-window, low-impact burn alerts to severity: ticket
- exclude probe/internal traffic from burn rules
- add dashboard panel and annotation showing top affected tenants and recent deploys

jamal: I'll open a CR to apply the alert rule changes and include tests in CI to prevent regressions. CR: CR-4021. will roll in maintenance window unless we need hotpatch now.
alex: can we hotpatch the probe exclusion right now?
jamal: yes — doing a hotpatch to the alert query to add traffic_type!="probe". will push in 2m.
(2 minutes)
jamal: hotpatch applied. alert noise should drop. please acknowledge if you see any missed pages.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: New alert firing suppressed due to updated rule: SLOBurn_Inference_MultiWindow evaluated -> severity=ticket (no page)
alex: good. next steps/tickets:
- JAMAL: CR-4021 apply full multi-window rule + tests (assignee: jamal)
- MARIA: DOC-118 update runbook with new tenant-targeted paging criteria and dashboard links (assignee: maria)
- TAYLOR: DASH-77 add panel for eu-west embeddings top tenants (assignee: taylor)
- PRODUCT-OPS: COMM-21 coordinate support messages to the 3 tenants (assignee: product-ops)

maria: postmortem notes: probable root = transient KV cache pressure combined with a traffic pattern spike from two tenants. recommend adding cache metrics to the embeddings dashboard and an alert for cache-miss rate > X.
jamal: +1; also recommend adding a short-lived autoscale config to pre-empt these spikes — infra to evaluate.
product-ops: support ticket updates queued. we’ll follow up with customers and offer rate-limiting guidance if necessary.
alex: closing this thread in 2h after verification window. thanks all. :heart:
